# The Simpsons (MAME set 'simpsons', 4 Players World, set 1) - 053248 program symbols
#
# Addresses and names only: no game data lives in this file.
# Format:  ADDRESS  KIND  NAME  [LAYOUT]   [# comment]
#   KIND: func = function entry, code = code label, data = data label
# Addresses are places of the program: offsets in its 512 KB region (tools/simpsons_rom.py), as kref's traces
# give them: a bank's code at bank x 2000 plus its address in the window (6000-7FFF), the fixed program (8000-FFFF)
# at 078000-07FFFF.
#
# LAYOUT, for data tables that hold code addresses the analysis cannot see the length of
# (tools/core/konami_cpu/analysis.py reads record=, code= and count=):
#   record=N        the table is an array of N-byte records
#   count=N         ... of N records
#   code=A          every record holds a 16-bit code address (a CPU address, in the table's bank) at offset A
# Sizes, offsets and counts are decimal.
#
# The analysis starts at the vectors (the reset at 86CE, the IRQ at 8F43, the FIRQ at 91B2) and finds the code
# without traces, following what the registers and the bank hold into the tables of handlers; the lines here are
# what it cannot work out, each with how it was found (kref --jumps: where a jump through a register went).

# ======== tables of code addresses ========
# two pairs of handler tables by an object's state (its field 2E), each followed by another table of code addresses
# that the code names (LDY #$7A3A, LDY #$7F7C, handed to a routine as data): the analysis stops a table where the
# code names data, but the state runs into the next table, whose first entry is the last state's
# bank 1D's: 629A "LDY #$7A00", 6292 "JMP [A,Y]" (kref --jumps: 03A292 -> 03A5DF, entry 29, which is 7A3A's first)
03BA00  data  bank_1d_states  record=2 count=30 code=0
# bank 1E's: 76FD "LDY #$7F62", 7700 "JMP [A,Y]" (kref --jumps: 03D700 -> 03D88C, entry 13, which is 7F7C's first)
03DF62  data  bank_1e_states  record=2 count=14 code=0

# ======== the sprite engine's data (tools/data_walk.py walks what these lead to) ========
# An object's animations (data_walk.py: animation sets): the bank they are in and the offset of the set's entry in
# that bank's set index, the words at 6000 (079B08-079B1B: "LDB ,U+; STB <$0E; SETLN <$0E; LDB ,U", then 079B3E
# "LDU #$6000; CLRA; LDU D,U")
struct animation_set 02 rom
field animation_set 00 bank u8
field animation_set 01 index u8
# by an object's kind (its field 04; 079B02): 00-7F here, 80-FF in animation_sets_high (bit 7 dropped): 079B08
# "LDU #$E591", 079B21 "LDU #$E5BB"; the reads stop at 07E5B9 (kref --rom-reads, 079B11), and 07E66B, right after the
# high ones, is the table 079E7F jumps through
07E591  table  animation_sets[21]  animation_set
07E5BB  table  animation_sets_high[88]  animation_set
# the sprite under a player in the air (079DFE, a sprite of its own after the object's: field 5B's low 4 bits the
# record, 079E0D "LDU #$E585", "ASLA; ASLA; LEAU A,U"): its attributes (079E19 "LDA ,U+") and its code (079E2B
# "LDD ,U"); byte 3 nothing reads
struct shadow_sprite 04 rom
field shadow_sprite 00 attributes u8
field shadow_sprite 01 code u16
07E585  table  shadow_sprites[3]  shadow_sprite
# a zoomed object's sprites (079CD4): their x and y from the object times a step by the object's zoom (its field 0A,
# from 10: 079CE1-079CED; 079D06 "LDB #$1D; STB <$0E; SETLN <$0E", 079D10 "LDX $602A", 079D17 "LDX D,X", then LMUL):
# the address of the steps in bank 1D's header, after its jumps, and the 240 steps (kref --rom-reads: 079D17 reads
# 03BDE7-03BFC6)
03A02A  table  zoom_steps_address[1]  u16
03BDE7  table  zoom_steps[240]  u16

# ======== the background maps (tools/data_walk.py: scene tables) ========
# A tile layer of the K052109 the map engine draws (07C618 "LDX #$EC9D; ASLA; LDX A,X": layer A's, layer B's): where
# its tiles are, the addresses of the variables its scroll is in, and its scene tables
struct layer_map 12 rom
# the layer's tile codes in the K052109 (07C621 "LDU ,X"; its colours 2000 below: 07C6C8 "STB #$-2000,U")
field layer_map 00 tiles u16
# the work RAM's variables, by address: its scroll (07C623 "LDD [#$02,X]", 07C633 "LDD [#$04,X]") and what the engine
# adds to it (07C5A5 "ADDD [#$0A,X]", 07C636 "ADDD [#$0C,X]", 07C6A4 "ADDD [#$0E,X]")
field layer_map 02 scroll_x u16
field layer_map 04 scroll_y u16
# (with its type, in the section of the program's data by name below: layer_map.maps, layer_map.unk_08)
field layer_map 0A offset_x u16
field layer_map 0C offset_y u16
field layer_map 0E offset_y2 u16
# (with its type, in the section of the program's data by name below: layer_map.maps_high, layer_maps)
07ECA1  table  layers[2]  layer_map
# by scene (direct page 75: 00-7F the first table, 80-FF the high one, bit 7 dropped), the address of a list of
# 4-byte records by the scene's area (direct page 76): an address and its bank. Layer A's maps from its descriptor
# (07C5B2 "LDY #$06,X", 07C5BA "LDY #$10,X", the descriptor ECA1 by 07C618 "LDX #$EC9D"), its tile blocks from
# 07C8BD "LDY #$ECC9" / 07C8C5 "LDY #$ED29"; layer B's from ECB3 and 07C8F7 "LDY #$ECE9" / 07C8FF "LDY #$EDBB".
# Each table ends where the first of its lists starts
# (with its type, in the section of the program's data by name below: block_scenes_a, block_scenes_b, map_scenes_a,
# map_scenes_b, block_scenes_a_high, block_scenes_b_high, map_scenes_a_high, map_scenes_b_high)
# the K052109's registers 1D80 and 1F00 by scene and area (07C931 "LDY #$EF55" / 07C939 "LDY #$EF63": 2-byte records)
# (with its type, in the section of the program's data by name below: layer_modes, layer_modes_high)
# 16 bytes by a tile block's second byte (07C6FA "LDX #$F67C"), copied a column at a time (07C70F)
07F67C  table  block_tile_flags[1]  u8

# (with its type, in the section of the program's data by name below: palette_sets, palette_sets_high)

# ======== the stages' objects (tools/data_walk.py: spawn lists) ========
# an object a stage puts in when its scroll reaches it (07C9B2-07CA4D, the list's place kept in direct page 73)
struct spawn 08 rom
# where along the stage (07C9DE "CMPD #$00,X" against the scroll plus 150); a record whose first byte is FF ends the
# list
field spawn 00 x u16
# its height, 8 pixels a step up from the floor line (07CA21 "LDB #$02,X; SEX; ASLDI #$03; NEGD")
field spawn 02 y s8
field spawn 03 depth u8
# bits 2-3 the object list it goes into (07CA50, by object_list_sizes and object_lists), bit 7 from the right
field spawn 04 flags u8
# the state the object starts in (07C9FE "LDA #$05,X; STA #$30,U": its field 30)
field spawn 05 state u8
# the stage's difficulty it takes (07C9E3 "CMPA <$6B": not put in above it)
field spawn 06 level u8
# the object's kind (07C9F5 "LDA #$07,X; STA #$01,U")
field spawn 07 kind u8
# by scene (07C96B "LDX #$EFBC; LDA <$67; ASLA; LDX [A,X]"): where in bank 1B the scene's list's address is
07EFBC  table  spawn_list_places[12]  u16
036000  table  spawn_lists[12]  u16
# by direct page 61 (07C985 "LDU #$EFD4; LDB <$61; LDB B,U"), times 2 into 1886
07EFD4  table  enemy_speeds_by_rank[32]  u8
# the object lists a spawn goes into, by its flags' bits 2-3 (07CA54 "LDU #$EFF4; LDA B,U", "LDU #$EFF8; LDU B,U"): how
# many objects each holds and where it is
07EFF4  table  object_list_sizes[4]  u8
07EFF8  table  object_lists[4]  u16

# ======== bank 1A's flying object (tools/data_walk.py: object paths) ========

struct path_step 02 rom

# by object_1a_path_choices (0353A7 "LDU #$79DC", by its field 50's low 3 bits): a path and the two counts it keeps
# in fields 3B and 3A (0353B9 "LDU #$79E4", "LEAU A,U" 4 bytes a record), and by the same index a time (0353CC "LDU
# #$79F0" into field 4F)

# ======== code nothing reaches ========
# runs nothing calls, jumps or points at that decode as instructions to a return or a jump (the coverage: unknown
# runs that decode to their end); each is code the game never runs, kept as it is

# the empty slots of jump tables (an LBRA to 0000: no routine), at a bank's start or in the fixed program's (0785xx
# on): nothing jumps through them
struct vector 03 rom
field vector 00 opcode u8
field vector 01 offset s16
0280BD  table  goon_actions_jump_table_spare_slot[1]  vector
02C030  table  scenery_jump_table_spare_slots[2]  vector
02C057  table  scenery_jump_table_spare_slot[1]  vector
032024  table  stage_7_objects_jump_table_spare_slot[1]  vector
07865F  table  fixed_jump_table_spare_slot_2[1]  vector
078665  table  fixed_jump_table_spare_slot_3[1]  vector
034000  table  dreamland_jump_table_spare_slots[2]  vector    # the first two slots of bank 1A's jump table
# a slot of the fixed program's jump table nothing jumps through, to a routine (07D47E) that dispatches by its object's
# field 28 like the objects' dispatchers (07D484 "LDU #$F661; LDB A,U; STB <$0E; SETLN <$0E", 07D496 "LDU #$F65F;
# ASLA; JMP [A,U]"), through tables that hold no code addresses there: F65F-F661 end a table of bytes, F662 starts
# one of code addresses (DDC3, DDF3...). Left from the game's making: its jump goes nowhere
0785D8  table  vector_to_dead_dispatch[1]  vector
07D49A  code  unused_enemy_run_action_jump  calls=unused_object_handlers
07F65F  data  unused_object_handlers  record=2 count=0 code=0
# a list of spawns no table leads to, in bank 1A: 67 records like a stage's (x from 0148 to 0540), no end record
0354C5  table  unused_dreamland_spawn_list[67]  spawn

# ======== the enemies (tools/data_walk.py: enemy behaviour) ========
# an enemy's behaviour, 88 bytes: what the fixed program's enemy routines (07D3D7-07D662) read from the object's field
# 2A: by its state (field 30) 8 bytes a state, 3 on (07D604-07D624: thresholds against a random number and the next
# states), and from 28 on 4 ranges of 12 bytes (07D3E7-07D3FD: how far, the least and the most of field 2D)
struct enemy_behaviour 58 rom
field enemy_behaviour 00 states u8[40]
field enemy_behaviour 28 ranges u8[48]
# bank 18's enemy, by its state (field 30: 030137 "LDU #$79DA; LDA #$30,X; ASLA; ASLA; LEAU A,U"): its next state and
# its flags (030141 "LDD ,U"), and its behaviour (030154 "LDD #$02,U; STD #$2A,X")
struct behaviour_choice 04 rom
field behaviour_choice 00 state u8
field behaviour_choice 01 flags u8
field behaviour_choice 02 behaviour u16 enemy_behaviour
0319DA  table  object_18_behaviours[5]  behaviour_choice

# ======== the decompiled program's files ========
# where the C of the 053248's functions goes (tools/decompile.py: src/PATH.c): a file line takes the functions from
# its place up to the next file line. Provisional, but for the boot and the interrupts: a file a bank, and the fixed
# program a file each 2000 bytes, until the functions are sorted by subject
0786CE  file  system/boot    # the reset: the board set up, the RAM and ROM checks, the main loop that runs the jobs
078F43  file  system/interrupts    # the IRQ's handler (the K052109's, at VBLANK: the inputs, the coin counters, the jobs) and the FIRQ's (the sprite DMA's)

# ======== functions the board puts its own in place of ========
# (runtime/replaced.txt, runtime/src/board_game.c)
# 078E5B (a bank in the window) and 078E63 (the fixed program) run into it: "LDD <$FA; ADDB ,X+; ADCA #$00; STD <$FA;
# LEAU -1,U; CMPU #$0000; BNE": the boot's RAM ROM CHECK adds up the program's chips, which the game does not have
078E68  func  add_rom_bytes

# ======== the program's data by name: the tables the C reads, and what it reads through pointers ========
# every table the decompiled 053248 program reads, by what it is, with its element type and count, and the records and
# values it reads through pointers (struct, elements, and the local and param lines that type the pointers); the
# evidence
# above each: the instructions that read it (as the listing has them) and what the value goes to. kref: what kref
# --rom-reads saw an instruction read in the scenarios

# ======== banks 10, 11, 12, 13 ========
# Places are offsets of the program region; "(cpu XXXX)" is the address the code names. Evidence quotes are the
# listing's (build\listing\simpsons.s); "kref" is build\reads\<scenario>\rom_reads.txt.
#
# Who is who (evidence for the subjects used below):
# - bank 10 holds the two bonus stages and the wrestler. Bonus 1: scene 83 (07A689 sets direct page 75 to 83), its
#   steps 020009 (from 07A6CC) and 020000 (from 07A748); bonus 2: scene 8B (07AF5A), 02000C (from 07AF97) and 020003
#   (from 07B00F); both end with the results at 020F39 (020207 "LBSR $6F39", 020BF0 "LBSR $6F39"). The bonus objects
#   are 4A40 + C0 x player (the player's slot: 0 Marge, 1 Homer, 2 Bart, 3 Lisa) with partners at +60 and +840.
#   (kind_0E.png shows the texts "Hey, wake up and find Maggie!" and "Blow up your balloon and go after Maggie!":
#   bonus 1's object grows as the player presses (its zoom, below), bonus 2 raises a level; the names keep
#   bonus_1 / bonus_2.)
# - the wrestler: object type 1F (the 4F80 list's handlers F2EC, entry 1F -> 020006 -> 0212F8), its kind 94 (021768 "LDU
#   #$7E79; ASLA; LDD A,U; ORB #$80; STD #$04,X", values 94xx; SET_NAMES 0x94 "wrestler"); stage 1's spawn list
#   (spawn_lists[0], 03659D) holds a type-1F spawn, stage 4's two, stage 8's one.
# - the krusty balloon: object type 05 (entry 05 -> 026000 -> 026509), its kind 9D (02696B "LDU #$7CB6", values
#   9Dxx; SET_NAMES 0x9D "krusty_balloon"); stage 2's spawn list (03685D) holds a type-05 spawn.
# - stage 7's boss: object type 37 (entry 37 -> 022009 -> 022A4C), kind A3 (022EA0 "LDU #$7A55", values A3xx;
#   no SET_NAMES name); the only type-37 spawn is in spawn_lists[9] (037A1D), scene 9 = step 13, stage 7. Its 4
#   helpers are type 37 of the second object list (5280; 07CB9F's handlers F40D, entry 37 -> 02200C -> 023171), kind 12.
# - the three bosses share one plan: health in field 1B (07C274 "LDA #$1B,X", 07C277 "SUBA #$1C,U": the attacker's
#   field 1C is the damage), a 5-piece gauge drawn by 0786BF (07E496: "STD <$E8" the health one piece stands for,
#   07E4AF "LDB #$05; MUL", 07E4B5 "LDB #$56,X" the health at the start, 07E4CD "CMPA <$EE" counting the pieces up to
#   5), and their target player in field 2B.

# ======== bank 11: the name entry and the high scores ========
# a player's record in the name entry (25 bytes), by player (02203D / 022079 "LDY #$7532", 022279 / 0222D9 "LDU

# - 0A the controls the player holds (4843 + 4 x player, 079248 "STA #$03,X": 02237B "LDA [#$0A,U]; ANDA #$02")

# - 0E the address of its repeat countdown (3868 + player: 022367 "LDA [#$0E,U]; DEC [#$0E,U]", 022382 "LDA #$0F; STA

# 022730 prints a letter as a sprite (code, x, y, colour in the sprite RAM: 022757-02278C): 022734 "LDX #$7695",
# 022737 "SUBA #$30", 022739 "LDB A,X" the code's low byte, 02273B "LDA #$-01,X" its high byte (78). Letters 30-80

# ======== banks 14, 15, 16, 17: the stages' goons, fat goons and scenery objects ========
#
# How the objects were told apart (evidence common to the entries below):
# - An object's type is its field 01; the dispatcher of list 0 (07CB6C "LDU #$F387; LDD #$01,X; LDB A,U; STB <$0E;
#   SETLN <$0E", 07CB7E "LDU #$F2EC; ASLA; JSR [A,U]") and those of lists 1-3 (07CBAD/07CBBF F4B0/F40D, 07CBE0/07CBF2
#   F54C/F4F4, 07CC0F/07CC21 F581/F577) pick the bank and the handler; "list N type T" below is that. The scenes a type
#   is put in come from the stages' spawn lists (spawn_lists by <$67: scene 0 stage 1, 1 stage 2, 3/4 stage 3
#   forest/cemetery, 5 stage 4, 6 stage 5, 8 stage 6, 9 stage 7, 11 stage 8; E88D[step]) with the list in the spawn's
#   flags bits 2-3 (07CA50 "ANDB #$0C; LSRB; LSRB").
# - Kinds (field 04, the sprite set, tools/extract_assets.py SET_NAMES) come from the object setups the handlers load
#   (07D132: "LDD ,U; ORB #$80; STD #$04,X"): 0785F9 -> 07D416 "LDU #$F1A8" (setup 8001: goon), bank 14's 7E5D (8401:
#   goon_with_hat), 7E6F (8201: goon_with_umbrella), 7E81 (8301: goon_with_shovel), bank 15's 764C/77C6 (8101/8100:
#   fat_goon). Kinds SET_NAMES leaves as kind_XX are named kind_XX here too.
# - Object fields used as evidence (checked in the listing): 0C x (and 0E its fraction), 0F x speed, 11 y, 14 y speed,
#   16 z (height: 07D16E's gravity "SUBD #$0060" from 19 brings it down to the floor in 5C), 19 z speed (the mover
#   0799A7-079A2A adds 0F to 0C-0E, 14 to 11-13, 19 to 16-18); 09 sprite attributes (bit 6 facing, 07D249; bits 4-5 the
#   priority 078638 returns with the floor); 3B/3C countdowns; 3E a word the handlers compare the object's x with
#   (028982 "LDD #$0C,X; CMPD #$3E,X") or a direction and speed (028672 "LDD #$3E,X; LBSR $8617": 07CC8E speeds from
#   A = direction, B = speed); 5C-5D the floor height (078638 -> 079495: the floor map cell at the object, low nibble x8
#   into 5D, bits 4-5 the priority, bit 7 no floor); 1874 the players present (07D301 skips the nearest-player search
#   when it is 0); 1884 set by the police car when it stops (02B489 "STA $1884").
# - An enemy's action is its field 28: 07D62C "LDD #$28,X; LDU #$F586" (fixed) and 07D64C "LDU #$F620" (bank) /
#   07D65E "LDU #$F5A2" (handler) dispatch it; enemy_behaviour's ranges name the action by the x distance to the
#   player (field 2D, 07D35B), e.g. goon_with_shovel's (029DE7): 01-23 action 33, 26-3A action 14, 3C-64 action 15.

# ======== banks 18, 19, 1A, 1B, 1C ========
# How the objects of these banks were told apart: the object lists' dispatchers (07CB6C "LDU #$F387" / 07CB7E "LDU
# #$F2EC" for 4F80, 07CBAD/07CBBF F4B0/F40D for 5280, 07CBE0/07CBF2 F54C/F4F4 for 4D40) give each type (field 01) a
# bank and a handler, and the enemies' actions (field 28) go through 07D64C "LDU #$F620" / 07D65E "LDU #$F5A2" the
# same way. Bank 18: 4F80 types 10, 11, 14, 21, 22, 23, 24, 2F, 31, F2, F5; 5280 types 18, 19, 1D, 20, 22; actions 19,
# 1A, 1D, 21, 22, 26, 2C, 31, 35, 3C. Bank 19: 4F80 types 30, 32, 33, 3D, FC, FD; 5280 types 33, 39, 3A, DE, F3, F5, F6,
# FB; 4D40 17, 19; actions 23-25, 28, 2A, 2B, 2D-30, 32, 37, 39-3B. Bank 1A: 4F80 F7, F8, FE, FF; 5280 E3, EA, FE, FF;
# 4D40 20, FE, FF. Bank 1B: 5280 types 0B, 0C, 12, 2A, 38. Bank 1C: the players (038003: the objects 4A40, 4B00, 4BC0,
# 4C80 with their records 49D0-49E8, the inputs from direct page 40-4E).
# Who each object is: its kind (field 04, the sprite set) from its setup (07D132 "LDD ,U; ORB #$80; STD #$04,X"), named
# as tools/extract_assets.py's SET_NAMES names the set (lumberjack 8D, gorilla 9F, knight BC-C1, robot 8F, hit_sparks
# 04); a set SET_NAMES does not name is called kind_XX, as extract_assets names its sheet. Its stage from the spawn
# lists (spawn_lists by scene, E88D: scene 0 stage 1, 1 stage 2, 3/4 stage 3, 5 stage 4, 6 stage 5, 8 stage 6, 9 stage
# 7, 11 stage 8). Object fields used below, checked in the listing: 05 animation, 06 bit 0 animation ended (079B90), 07
# the animation's frame (079B3B "INC #$07,X", 079B6D), 09 flags (bit 6 faces left), 0A/0B zoom, 0C x, 11 y, 16 height,
# 0F/14/19 the x, y and height speeds (07D16E "SUBD #$0060" on 19: gravity; 07CCDD sets 14 and 0F from a direction),
# 1F/20/21 the hit box's sizes and 22/23/24 its offsets (07C13A-07C1D7), 1B vitality, 30 the state a spawn gives it
# (07C9FE "LDA #$05,X; STA #$30,U"), 3B a countdown.

# ---- shared shapes ----
# a child object, the record 07862C/07CA8A puts in at an offset from the object in X (by Y): its x offset, negated
# when X faces left (07CAB1-07CAC6), its y and height offsets (07CAD2 "ADDD #$11,X", 07CADC "LDB #$04,Y; ADDD
# #$16,X"), the object list (07CA8A "LDB #$05,Y; LBSR $CA54"), its state and type (07CA92 "LDD #$06,Y; STA #$30,U;
# STB #$01,U").

field child_object 06 state u8

# an x speed and a y speed (fields 0F and 14), read as a pair (0311C2 "LDD ,U; STD #$0F,X", 0311C7 "LDD #$02,U; STD
# #$14,X"; 039894 "LDD ,Y++; STD #$0F,U")
struct velocity 04 rom
field velocity 00 x_speed s16
field velocity 02 y_speed s16
# a height of a bobbing wave, read by a pointer the code points at one of two tables (031184/0335E1: "LDB B,U; SEX")
elements bob_height s8

# ======== banks 1D, 1E, 1F, 20, 2F ========
#
# Who is who (evidence used by many entries below):
# - The 4F80 list's dispatcher (07CB3C: "LDU #$F387; LDB A,U; SETLN; LDU #$F2EC; ASLA; JSR [A,U]") sends type F6 to bank
#   1D 6000 (03A271), type EC to 1D 6009 (03A99E), EA to 1D 6024 (03B8D8), and in bank 1E type 19 to 6000 (03C348), 20
#   to 6009 (03C8BC), 0B to 600C (03CE4D), 3E to 6018 (03D1B3), F9 to 601B (03D6ED), E8 to 6015 (03DB61).
#   (07EFF4/07EFF8: a spawn's flags bits 2-3 pick the list: 0 4F80, 1 5280, 2 4D40, 3 5640; each list has its own
#   dispatcher and type tables, so a type number means an object only within its list.)
# - spawn_lists by scene (E88D[step]: scene 05 = step 8 stage 4, 06 = step 9 stage 5, 08 = step 11 stage 6, 0B = step
#   15 stage 8): scene 0B's list puts in F6 and EC (both x 03E0, flags 00), scene 05's a 19 at 0870, scene 06's a 20 at
#   0828, scene 08's eight F9 (0290-02E0).
# - "stage_8_boss" = type F6 (bank 1D 03A271): kind 9C (03A2AA "LDA #$9C; STA #$04,X"; set 9C is unnamed), health in
#   field 1B (80, refilled while field 2D > 0: 03A277-03A288), three phases by field 2D (03A37A "LDY #$7A9C; JMP
#   [A,Y]"), and its defeat advances the step's sub-step (03A794 "INC <$04"); 07B333-07B354 then runs a story and sets
#   <$81, which type EC waits for (03AD6B "LDA <$81"). It is the boss before Mr. Burns' robot.
# - "burns_robot" = type EC (bank 1D 03A99E): kinds CC-D4 (burns_robot..burns_robot_5 in SET_NAMES: 03AA88 "LDD
#   #$D489", the table 03BBF9), its parts object_1d_parts include kind D3 (mr_burns). Field 30 + field 34 is its form
#   (0-4: 03AAE5 "LDA #$30,X; ADDA #$34,X").
# - "football_player" (type 19, kind 92: 03C35C), "bear" (type 20, kind A2: 03C8CD): SET_NAMES names; both end their
#   stage's step ("INC <$04": the football player's at 03C79F, the bear's at 03CD59), stage 4 and stage 5 (kref
#   --rom-reads: only the stage4 / stage5 scenarios read their tables).
# - "stage_3_boss" = type 3E (bank 1E 03D1B3): two of them, kind C4 (field 30 = 0) and C3 (field 30 = 1: the first puts
#   in the second, 03D1C5 "LDY #$7F08; LBSR $862C", child record type 3E), field 41 links them; when both are gone
#   03D509-03D50E "STA <$7D; INC <$04"; only the stage3 scenario reads their tables. Bank 13 puts the first in
#   (0260FD "LDA #$3E; STA #$01,U").
# - Object field 00 bit 04 = can not be hurt: 07C26D "LDA #$00,X; ANDA #$04; BNE" skips "SUBA #$1C,U" (the health
#   loss) and "ORA #$20" (hit). Field 1B the health, 1C the damage an object deals, 1D the strength it hits with (into
#   the victim's 1E).
# - Tables by the players in the game read "LDA <$57; LDA A,Y" (no DECA) have entries 1-4: their entry 4 is the next
#   table's first byte (the game's own tables share it); counts kept at the piece's length where a piece starts there.

# the coinage settings: by the coin setting the work RAM keeps at 59F1 (the EEPROM's settings' copy: 078A1A "LDX
# #$59F1", 078A1D "LDU #$E3EB", 078A20 "LDA ,X", 078A22 "LDA A,U"), a byte whose high nibble is the coins a credit
# takes (078A30-078A34 "LSRA" x4, "STA <$1C"; 07921E "LDA <$1C", 079229 "CMPA #$02,U" against the coins counted) and
# whose low nibble the credits they give (078A26 "ANDA #$0F; STA <$1D"; 079239 "LDB <$1D; ADDD #$00,U"): 11 12 13 ...

# the sums the RAM ROM CHECK expects of the program's four chips (MAME's ROM_START( simpsons ): 13c at 040000, 15c at
# 060000, 16c at 000000, 17c at 020000), each compared with the sum of 078E5B/078E63 (direct page FA) and printed OK
# or BAD (078C4F "LDB #$03"): banks 20-2F (078C22 "LDA #$20", 078C3D "CMPA #$30", 078C46 "CMPD $E423"); the fixed
# program and banks 30-3B (078C61 "LDX #$8000; LDU #$8000; LBSR $8E63", 078C6A "LDA #$30", 078C85 "CMPA #$3C",
# 078C8E "CMPD $E425"); banks 00-0F (078CA9 "LDA #$00", 078CC4 "CMPA #$10", 078CCD "CMPD $E427"); banks 10-1F

# and 078DB9 "JMP [$FFFE]"): 86CE, the reset's routine. It is the last word of the CPU's vectors (FFF6 FIRQ 91B2,
# FFF8 IRQ 8F43, FFFA SWI and FFFC NMI 89EC, FFFE RESET 86CE; FFF0-FFF5 FF), which today sit at the end of the

# ======== the players ========

# a player's record (07A0DE "LDU #$E819; LDA <$F0; ASLA; LDU A,U", 07B713 "LDX #$E819 ... LDX A,X", by the player's
# number): the addresses of its variables in the work RAM, read through ([#$NN,X]) by the players' routines
# 07B731-07B8B0 (by its state, 07B71B "LDY #$E803", 07B71E "LDA [#$17,X]; ASLA; JSR [A,Y]") and by the attract's demo
# (07A0E7-07A114). Marge's record: 4842 481E 49D1 01 4A00 49D4 "MRG" 00 49D2 4840 4A5B 4A44 49D7 49F0; each next player
# 4 on
# for 00 and 11, 8 on for 02 04 09 0F 17, 7 on for 07, C0 on for 13 and 15 (its object), 1 on for 19
struct player 1B rom
# its newly pressed controls (4842 + 4 x player: 07924D-079265 keep each player's controls at 4840 + 4n, last frame's
# at +1, the newly pressed at +2, the held at +3): 07B75C "LDA [,X]; ANDA #$B0" (start and the two buttons: it joins)
field player 00 pressed u16
# the flag its coin slot's record keeps once the slot has given it a credit (481E = the record 4817 + 8n's byte 7:
# 079242 "LDA #$01; STA #$07,U"; while it is clear a credit takes direct page 3A's coins more, 079221 "LDB #$07,U; BNE;
# ADDA <$3A"), cleared when the player leaves the game (07B88B and 07B9E3 "CLR [#$02,X]")
field player 02 credit_given u16
field player 04 lives u16
field player 06 bit u8
# its continue countdown: BCD seconds then frames (07B82D "LDA #$20; STA [#$07,X]"; 07B86E "LDY #$07,X; INC #$01,Y;
# CMPA #$3C" a second, "LDA #$99; ADDA ,Y; DAA" down by one), and the game-over wait's frames (07B89D "INC [#$07,X];
# LDA [#$07,X]; CMPA #$C0")
# its score, a BCD word (49D4 + 8n): the score jobs 03-06 add to it (079828 "LDX #$49D4; LBRA $96FD" ... 07983A "LDX
# #$49EC"), 07B7B6 "LDD [#$09,X]" checks it against the high scores (079718: the 10 records at 4983) when it leaves
field player 09 score u16
# its initials for the high score table: MRG, HMR, BRT, LSA (07B7C6 "LDD #$0B,X; STD <$F0", 07B7CC "LDA #$0D,X; STA
# <$F2", copied into the high score record by 079743-079779)
field player 0B initial_1 u8
field player 0C initial_2 u8
field player 0D initial_3 u8
field player 0E number u8
# its life the game keeps between stages (49D2 + 8n): 07B7A5 "LDA #$28; STA [#$0F,X]" when it joins, 07B6B6-07B6C3
# "LDA #$28; STA ,U" for each player playing at a stage's start, 020A17-020A21 "ADDA #$14 ... CMPA #$28" a refill
field player 0F life u16
# its controls block (4840 + 4n: this frame, last frame, newly pressed, held: 07924D-079265); nothing reads it through
# the record
field player 11 controls u16
# its object's hit points (the player object 4A40 + C0 x player's field 1B, which 07C2E0 "LDA #$1B,X; SUBA #$1C,U"
# lowers by the hitter's power): 07B7A8 "STA [#$13,X]" (28) when it joins
field player 13 object_life u16
# its object's kind (field 04, the sprite set): 07A0EC "LDA <$F0", 07A0EF "STA [#$15,U]" (07A174-07A177 likewise
# through X): the player's number (00 marge, 01 homer, 02 bart, 03 lisa)
field player 15 object_kind u16
# its state (49D7 + 8n), by which 07B71E "LDA [#$17,X]; ASLA; JSR [A,Y]" runs the routines at E803: 0 out (07B731:
# credits make it 1), 1 may join (07B74F: start with a credit, lives from direct page 5A, then 2), 2 playing (07B7E8:
# no lives left makes it 3, 07B83F), 3 the continue countdown (07B843: a credit makes it 5, the countdown's end 4),
# 4 game over (07B897: C0 frames, then 0), 5 joining again (07B74F)
field player 17 state u16
# whether it plays (49F0 + n): 2 playing (07B7DF, 07B7EA), 1 while its continue countdown runs (07B83A, 07B845),
# 0 neither (07B731 "CLR [#$19,X]"); 07B8BA-07B8D8 and 07B901-07B922 "LDA $49F0; CMPA #$02" (anyone playing),
# 07B6BB "LDA ,X; CMPA #$02" (the life refilled at a stage's start)
field player 19 play_status u16

# the addresses of the players' newly pressed controls (4842, 4846, 484A, 484E: the same as each player record's
# field 00): 07979A "LDX #$E449", 07979D "LDA <$F0; ASLA", 0797A1 "LDA [A,X]; ANDA #$30" (the two buttons) for each
# player whose bit is in direct page 50 (07978C "LDB <$50", 4 of them: 079792 "CMPA #$04"): any of them skips (a story);
# kref: 0797A1 reads 07E449-07E450
07E449  table  player_presses[4]  u16

# what the score jobs add to a player's score (by the job's argument B): 0796FF "LDU #$E445", 079702 "ASLB", 079703
# "LEAU B,U", 079705 "LDA #$01,U; ADDA #$01,X; DAA; STA #$01,X", 07970F "LDA ,U; ADCA ,X; DAA; STA ,X": a BCD word
# (0000, 0001) added to the score at X (the jobs 03-06 of the main loop's job table E3FB: 0789E4 "LDX #$E3FB; ASLA;
# JSR [A,X]", entries 079828-07983A).
struct score_addition 02 rom
field score_addition 00 high u8
field score_addition 01 low u8
07E445  table  score_additions[2]  score_addition

# ======== the attract's demos ========
# demos holds the demos' addresses (07A0A4 "LDX #$E6A1; LDA <$5E; ASLA; LDX A,X") each a demo record; the
# players' inputs are a field a player (07A0D2 "LDY #$5810", 07A0F2 "LDU ,X++" once for each of the 4 players, 07A0F4
# "STU ,Y", Y 10 on a
# player: 07A117), each the address in bank 2C (07A0C8 "LDB #$2C; STB <$0E; SETLN <$0E") of that player's inputs
07E6A1  table  demos[3]  u16 demo
struct demo 0C rom
field demo 00 players u8
field demo 01 frames u16
field demo 03 step u8
field demo 04 marge_inputs u16 demo_input
field demo 06 homer_inputs u16 demo_input
field demo 08 bart_inputs u16 demo_input
field demo 0A lisa_inputs u16 demo_input
# (in the same function) the input step 07A0F2 loads, read 07A0F6 "LDA #$01,U" (its frames) and
# 07A0FC "LDA ,U" (its controls); and the player record 07A101 "PULLS U" brings
# back (07A103 "CLR [#$04,U]", 07A114 "STA [#$17,U]")

# ======== the steps and scenes ========

# the scene of each step of the game: 07BA87 "LDX #$E88D", 07BA8A "LDA <$03", 07BA8D "LDA A,X", 07BA8F "STA <$67"
# (steps 2 and 3, stage 1 and its bonus, scene 0; 4 stage 2 scene 1; 6-7 stage 3 scenes 3-4; 8 4 scene 5... 15 stage 8
# scene 0B; 12, bonus 2, scene 0); kref: 07BA8D reads 07E88F-07E89C (steps 2-15)
07E88D  table  step_scenes[16]  u8

# the objects' sprites' priority against the tile layers, by the step (all 05): 079ADD "LDX #$E574", 079AE0 "LDA
# <$03", 079AE3 "LDA A,X", 079AE5 "STA <$FA"; an object without its own (field 09 bits 4-5 clear: 079DE2-079DE7) takes
# it (079DF7 "LDA <$FA; STA <$FB"), into its sprites' colour word's high byte (079C18 "LDA <$FB", 079C29 "STD #$0C,Y"),
# which the K053246's callback in simpsons.cpp takes as the priority ((color & 0x0f80) >> 6); kref: 07E574-07E584
07E574  table  step_sprite_priorities[17]  u8

# a routine in bank 1F each scene runs while its stage plays: by the scene (07B5B6 "LDX #$E7D3", 07B5B9 "LDA <$67",
# 07B5BC "ASLA; ASLA; LEAX A,X"), its bank (07B5C2 "LDB ,X+; STB <$0E; SETLN <$0E") and the routine (07B5CC "JSR
# [,X]"), in the steps' playing substep (07A5E0 "LBRA $B5A9", substep 3 of step 2's table E707). Bank 1F's put the
# actor at 5640 to a story script (03E804 "LDX #$5640; LDA #$38; STA #$30,X; LBRA $605A"; 03E05A starts it when the
# actor is free); scenes 2, 7 and 0A (the stories') have 07B6A4 ("CLRA; RTS"); byte 3 is 00 in all and nothing reads
# it. kref: 07B5C2 reads 07E7D3-07E7FF.
struct scene_routine 04 rom
field scene_routine 00 bank u8
field scene_routine 01 routine u16
field scene_routine 03 spare u8
07E7D3  table  scene_routines[12]  scene_routine

# ======== the palette jobs ========

# what a palette request starts, by its kind in direct page 7E (07BAC9 "LDX #$BADA", 07BACE "LDA <$7E", 07BAD1 "ASLA",
# 07BAD2 "LDX A,X", 07BAD6 "JSR ,X"): each takes a free slot of the jobs at 3C00 (07BF39: 40 of 8 bytes, run each frame
# by 07BC8B "LDX #$BCAA; ASLA; JSR [A,X]") and writes its job: 0 and 1 a load of palette sets (BAEC: job 1), 2 a
# palette effect from bank 2E (BB1F: job 2), 3 the background colour (BB71: job 3, which 07BDF6 "LDD #$01,U; STD
# $0C00" sets), 4 and 5 a fade of the ranges the request's bits name (BB85: job 4 darkens, 5 brightens), 6 the palette
# RAM's 0C00-0DFF filled with FFFF (BBF6: job 6), 7 a clear of palette ranges (BC78: job 7), 8 the effect again in
# the caller's slot when it runs one (BB12 "LDA ,U; CMPA #$02; BNE $BB1F"); kref: 07BAD2 reads 07BADC-07BAEB
07BADA  table  palette_request_handlers[9]  u16

# a palette effect's start, in bank 2E (07BB35 "LDB #$2E", 07BB37 "STB <$0E", 07BB3A "SETLN <$0E"), by the request's
# number D (07BB45 "LDX #$6000", 07BB48 "LDD <$E8; ASLB; ROLA", 07BB4D "LDX D,X"): after 2 bytes (07BB4F "LEAX
# #$02,X") the colours a step sets less one (07BB52 "LDA ,X+; STA #$06,U": 07BD51-07BD62 count it down to 0) and the
# frames between steps (07BB57 "LDA ,X+; STA #$04,U; STA #$05,U": 07BD0D "LDA #$04,U; CMPA #$05,U"), then the steps
# (07BB5F "STX #$02,U": address and colour, 4 bytes a colour). Byte 0 is 80, where a run backwards stops (07BD85 "LEAX
# #$-08,X; LDA ,X; BPL"); byte 1 nothing reads. The table at bank 2E's 6000: 146 bytes (kref: 07BB4D reads
# 05C000-05C091).
struct palette_effect 04 rom
field palette_effect 00 stop u8
field palette_effect 01 spare u8
field palette_effect 02 extra_colours u8
field palette_effect 03 delay u8
05C000  table  palette_effects[73]  u16 palette_effect
# a step of a palette effect's script, after its header: a colour's place in the palette RAM and the colour (07BD57
# "LDY ,X++; LDD ,X++; STD ,Y", the job's byte 6 more colours a step: 07BD51 "LDA #$06,U"), X the script's place, which
# the job keeps at its byte 2 (07BD67 "STX #$02,U"); 07BD6C the same, then back two steps to run them again
struct palette_effect_step 04 rom
field palette_effect_step 00 address u16
field palette_effect_step 02 colour u16

# the palette sets (already named) point at their loads (07BCDC "LDY B,X", 07BCEA "LDU ,Y", 07BCEC "LDX #$02,Y",
# 07BCEF "LDA #$04,Y", 07BCF5 "LEAY #$05,Y"): the tables get the struct
07E9CB  table  palette_sets[14]  u16 palette_load
07EAEB  table  palette_sets_high[19]  u16 palette_load
# 07BCBA keeps either table in X (07BCCE "LDX #$E9CB", or from 80 07BCD6 "LDX #$EAEB; ANDB #$7F") and reads 07BCDC
# "LDY B,X"
elements palette_set u16 palette_load

# the palette ranges a fade works on, one a step of the fade (the job's byte 7, 0-15: 07BE24 "CMPA #$10" starts it
# again): 07BE4D "LDX #$E97F", 07BE50 "LDA #$07,U; ASLA; ASLA; LEAX A,X", 07BE57 "LDA ,X+; STA <$F1" the colours,
# 07BE5C "LDU ,X" the first one's address in the palette RAM, each darkened or brightened (07BE5E "LDY #$E97B; LDA
# <$F0; ASLA; JSR [A,Y]": 07BF94 takes a step off each component, 07BFD1 adds one) a colour at a time (07BE67 "LEAU
# #$02,U; DEC <$F1"), when the job's mask has the step's bit (07BE34 "LDA #$06,U; ANDA #$01", 07BE71 "LSRW #$05,U";
# the mask from the request's bits, 07BB85-07BBF2: bit 0 steps 0-1, 1 steps 2-3, 2 steps 4-5, 3 steps 6-13, 4 step
# 14). 15 records: 32 colours at 0400 0440 0800 0840 0A00 0A40 0000 0040... 01C0, and 1 at 0C00; byte 3 is 00 in all,
# nothing reads it. kref: 07BE57/07BE5C read 07E987-07E9B9.
struct fade_range 04 rom
field fade_range 00 colours u8
field fade_range 01 address u16
field fade_range 03 spare u8
07E97F  table  fade_ranges[15]  fade_range

# the palette ranges job 7 clears, one a bit of the request (07BEFB "LDA #$01,U; STA <$F1", 07BF04 "ANDA #$01", 4 of
# them: 07BF24 "CMPA #$04"): 07BF08 "LDX #$E9BB", 07BF0B "LDA <$F0; ASLA; ASLA; LEAX A,X", 07BF12 "LDU ,X++" the bytes
# after the first, 07BF14 "LDX ,X" where, 07BF16 "LEAY ,X; CLR ,X+; BMOVE Y,X,U" (007F 0400, 007F 0800, 007F 0A00,
# 01FF 0000).
struct palette_clear 04 rom
field palette_clear 00 extra_bytes u16
field palette_clear 02 address u16
07E9BB  table  palette_clears[4]  palette_clear

# the palette effects an object's colours take as it loses its hit points (0786BF "LBRA $E496"): by the caller's B
# (07E4F1 "LDY #$E526", 07E4F4 "LDA <$E9; ASLA; LDY A,Y"; at the start 07E515 "LDU #$E526", 07E51C "LDD [A,U]", a new
# effect, 07E510 "LDA #$02; STA <$7E", its slot kept in field 54: 07E521 "STU #$54,X"), a row of 6 effect numbers by
# a level (07E4FA "LDA <$EA; ASLA; LDD A,Y", 07E500 "LBSR $BAC7" with 07E4EC "LDA #$08; STA <$7E": the effect again in
# its slot). The level is 0 when its hit points (field 1B, which 07C274 "LDA #$1B,X; SUBA #$1C,U" lowers by the
# hitter's power) are gone (07E49E "TST #$1B,X"), else 1-5 by how much of the last 5 x A of them is left (07E4AF-
# 07E4DD, A the caller's step by the players in the game, e.g. 021307 "LDU #$7E75; LDA <$57; DECA; LDA A,U"); 5 changes
# nothing (07E4DB "CMPB #$05; BNE"), and a level counts only below the last one (07E4E4 "CMPA #$53,X; BCC").
# Callers: bank 10's object B=0 (021310 "CLRB"), bank 13's B=1 (02652C), bank 1E's two B=2 (03C348) and B=3 (03C8BC),
# bank 11's B=4 (022A6A). kref: 07E4FE reads the first 5 words of each row, never the sixth
struct hurt_effect_row 0C rom
# at the start, and again when its hit points are gone
field hurt_effect_row 00 normal u16
field hurt_effect_row 02 fifth_left u16
field hurt_effect_row 04 two_fifths_left u16
field hurt_effect_row 06 three_fifths_left u16
field hurt_effect_row 08 four_fifths_left u16
# level 5, which changes nothing: never read
field hurt_effect_row 0A all_left u16
07E526  table  hurt_effect_rows[5]  u16 hurt_effect_row

# ======== the sprites' animations ========
# 079AE9 picks an object's animation set by its kind (field 04, 079B03 "LDB #$04,X"): 079B08 "LDU #$E591; ASLB; ROLA;
# LEAU D,U" (from 80, 079B21 "LDU #$E5BB"), the set's bank (079B11 / 079B2A "LDB ,U+; STB <$0E; SETLN <$0E") and its
# index's offset (079B1B / 079B34 "LDB ,U")
# then the set's table of animations from the index at the start of that bank (079B3E "LDU #$6000; CLRA", 079B42 "LDU
# D,U": data_walk.py's set index), and the animation by field 05 (079B69 "ASLB;
# ROLA", 079B6B "LDU D,U"), then the frame by field 07 (079B6D "LDA #$07,X; ASLA; ASLA; LEAU A,U"). The bank is
# whichever animation_sets gave, so the index is no table of its own: a pointer typed by the instruction that loads it
elements animation_set_index u16 animation_table
elements animation_table u16

# ======== the objects' dispatchers: the bank of each type's handler ========
# Each list of objects runs its objects' handlers by their type (field 01, signed: types run below 0): "LDD #$01,X",
# the bank "LDB A,U; STB <$0E; SETLN <$0E", the handler "ASLA; JSR [A,U]" from the table after. The handler tables
# (F2EC, F40D, F4F4, F577, F5A2) and the bank tables share the bytes: each bank table's negative types are the end of
# the handler table before it, and the bytes after its type 3F are the start of the next list's handler table for its
# negative types. Counts: the asset pieces' (each bank table and the handler words that follow it, up to the next table)
# the list at 4F80 (8 objects; spawn list 0, object_lists' first), the enemies: 07CB62 "LDX #$4F80", 07CB6C "LDU
# #$F387", 07CB74 "LDB A,U", 07CB7E "LDU #$F2EC; ASLA; JSR [A,U]", and each counted unless its field 42 has bit 7
# (07CB84-07CB89 "INC $1876", the count the enemy limits above hold the stage to); kref: 07CB74 reads 07F36D-07F3C6
# (types -26 to 3F); 07F3C7-07F40C are the next list's handlers for its types -35 to -1 (07CBC3 reads 07F3C7-07F48C)
07F387  table  enemy_banks[134]  u8

# (types -35 to 3F); 07F4F0-07F4F3 are the next list's handlers for its types -2 and -1 (07CBF6 reads 07F4F0-07F549).

# the animation an object shows in the fixed program's shared hit reaction (07865C "LBRA $E1D3": by field 29, 07E1D3
# "LDU #$F29E; LDA #$29,X; ASLA; JSR [A,U]"), by its field 28 (07E1FB "LDU #$F2AC", 07E1FE "LDA #$28,X", 07E205 / 07E239
# "LDA A,U; ORA #$80; STA #$05,X": field 05, started again); 0-1 stand (07E240 "CLRW #$0F,X"), 2 on are thrown back
# (07E20F "LDD #$0400; STD #$19,X", 07E215 "LDD #$FE00; STD #$0F,X"). kref: 07E239 reads 07F2AC-07F2AD, 07E205
# 07F2AE-07F2B5 (field 28 0-9). Count 10, not the piece's 64: 07F2B8 on is the enemies' handler table for their types
# -26 to -1 (F2EC less 2 x 26; 07CB82 reads 07F2B8-07F36B), and 07F2B6-07F2B7 (60 6F) look like one more handler word
# (type -27, whose bank byte 07F36C is 17) that no scenario reaches
07F2AC  table  hit_animations[64]  u8
# U holds the table's address (07E1FB) and, later, field 25's object (07E21B "LDU #$25,X"): the table's, typed
elements hit_animation u8

# ======== moving: the sines, the angle, the jumps ========
# a quarter of a sine wave, 0-90 degrees in 64 steps, 128 at 90 (sin x 128: 0, 3, 6 ... 5B at 32 ... 80 at 64):
# 07CCA0 "LDU #$F061", 07CCA3-07CCB0 fold the angle (0-FF, 40 = 90 degrees) to 0-40, 07CCB1 "LDA A,U", 07CCB6 "MUL"
# by the speed, 07CCB7 "LSRDI #$04", negated past 80 (07CCBE "NEGD"); 07CC8E puts the two (sine and, 40 on, cosine)
# into the speeds 14 and 0F; kref: 07CCB1 reads 07F061-07F0A1. (Read through U; its piece neighbours
# the next two)
07F061  table  sines[65]  u8
# the same quarter at 20 (sin x 20: 0 ... 0E at 32 ... 14 at 64), times 16 as a speed: 07CCC0 "LDU #$F0A2", 07CCD1 "LDB
# A,U; CLRA; ASLDI #$04" (07CCDD: fields 14 and 0F); kref: 07CCD1 reads 07F0A2-07F0E2
07F0A2  table  sines_20[65]  u8
# the arctangent, in 256ths of a turn, of 0-64 sixty-fourths (0 ... 20 at 64, 45 degrees): the direction from X's object
# to U's (07CCFD "LDD #$0C,U", 07CD00 "SUBD #$0C,X"; 07CD0A "LDD #$11,U", 07CD0D "SUBD #$11,X"): the shorter distance
# over the longer,
# both shifted so the longer fits in a byte (07CD1C-07CD3A), divided (07CD42 "DIV X,B"), the quotient the index (07CD43
# "LDD #$F0E3", 07CD46 "LDA D,X"; the other way 07CD71-07CD78 "LDA D,X; SUBA #$40; NEGA"), then the quadrant by the
# signs (07CD79-07CD8D); kref: 07CD46 reads 07F0E3-07F123. It is the second half of the piece 07F0A2
# (130 bytes): with sines_20 at 65 the piece's two tables are 65 and 65
07F0E3  table  arctangents[65]  u8
# the speed up (into field 19, 16 times this: 07CDE0 "LDB A,U; CLRA; ASLDI #$04", 07CDE5 "STD #$19,X"; 079A18-079A2A
# add it to the height in 16) an object jumps with to a floor N steps of 8 pixels above the one it is on: N = field 45
# (the floor the block flags give: 07CEB1 "ANDA #$0F; STA #$45,X"; 07CF0E "LDB #$45,X; ASLDI #$03; CMPD #$16,X") less
# field 5D / 8 (07CDD6 "LDB #$5D,X; LSRB x3"; 07CE13-07CE18 the floor x 8): 07CDD3 "LDU #$F124", 07CDDE "SUBA ,S+";
# from 07D6D6, 07D70F, 07D739, 07D763 (the actions 07D6C4-07D751, each with "LDA #$45,X" first). Entry 1 (90) is out
# of line with 2-15 (7A up by 2);
# kref: 07CDE0 reads 07F126-07F130
07F124  table  climb_speeds[16]  u8

# ======== the work RAM's structures ========
# An object: 0x60 bytes, 33 of them from 4A40 (the profile's STRUCT_ARRAYS): the 4 players' objects and their partners
# (4A40 + C0 x player, + 60), then the lists object_lists gives (4D40 x 6, 4F80 x 8, 5280 x 10, 5640 x 1). A field
# nothing names here is unk_XX in the C, at the width the code uses it most
struct object 60
# a free slot where 0 (the free-slot search 07CA5F "LDB #$00,U; BNE"); the dispatchers run the object where above 1
# (07CB65 "LDA #$00,X; CMPA #$01; BLS")
field object 00 flags u8
# the type the list's dispatcher runs it by: its handler's bank and address by the type, signed (07CB6F "LDD
# #$01,X", 07CB74 "LDB A,U": types below 0 run too)
field object 01 type s8

# ======== the engine ========
# Names for the fixed program's engine: 078000-079FFF (the jump table, the boot, the interrupts, the main loop's jobs,
# the text printers, the floor map, the sprite engine, the attract's first scenes) and 07E000-07FFFF (the enemies'
# shared reactions), and the common fields of struct object.
# symbols.txt syntax. Evidence: build/listing/simpsons.s (quoted as PLACE "INSTRUCTION"), the C of src/, the data in
# assets/data/ (texts.txt, tables.txt, objects.txt) and the existing notes of symbols.txt.
#
# Conventions of this part:
# - an object's place: 0C x, 11 y, 16 z (its height), as symbols.txt's child_object (dx dy dz), part (dx dy dz),
#   bluebird_launch (x_speed y_speed z_speed: 0F 14 19), test_player (x 0C, z 16) and velocity (x_speed, y_speed) have
#   them. y is the place on the floor (the sprites' y is y + z: 079C50-079C59), z the height above it.
# - the fixed program's jump table (078593-0786CB, an "LBRA" each, which the banks call): an entry that only jumps is
#   named vector_ + what its routine does (the routine itself, in 07A000-07DFFF, is named elsewhere; the names here
#   follow what the routine does). An entry the decompiler folded its
#   routine into (the routine has no other caller: its code is in the entry's C function) gets the routine's own name.
# - the enemies' shared reactions (field 28 the action, 29 its step) are named enemy_<reaction>_<step>, so each
#   reaction is a family.

# ======== the objects' common fields (struct object) ========
# What the engine reads the same way in every object: the dispatchers (07CB62-07CC2E), the free-slot search (07CA54),
# the spawn (07C9B2-07CA4D) and child spawn (07CA8A-07CAE9), the setup (07D132), the sprite engine (079841-079E38),
# the mover (0798F5), the depth sort (079A37), the hit checks (07C13A-07C366), the landing (07D16E-07D1B6) and the
# enemies' shared routines (07CFEC-07E2D6). Each line's evidence is above it. Offsets the engine uses one way for the
# players and another for the enemies (45, 46, 49) are left to the families (see the report).

# the state the type's handler runs: the dispatchers load "LDD #$01,X" (07CB6F, 07CBB0, 07CBE3, 07CC12) and hand B to
# the handler, which switches on it (bank 18's "ASLB; JSR [B,U]"); the free-slot search and the spawns start it at 0
# (07CA6C-07CA72 clears the slot, 07C9FB "CLRW #$02,U", 07CAAE "CLRW #$02,U"); the hit routines set FE/FF (07CFDD
# "LDA #$FE", 07CFE1 "LDA #$FF"), the enemies' hit check 4 (07D019 "LDD #$8004", 07D01F "STB #$02,X"), the climbs 5
# (07CF91 "LDA #$05; STA #$02,X")
field object 02 state u8
# its sprite set: the sprite engine picks the bank and the set of animations by it (079B03 "LDB #$04,X; BMI", 079B08
# "LDU #$E591" animation_sets, 079B21 "LDU #$E5BB" animation_sets_high); the setup gives it (07D13B "STD #$04,X" with
# its animation); 00-03 are the players (07CFB5 "LDA #$04,U; CMPA #$03; BHI": a hit by a player)
field object 04 kind u8
# its animation in the set: bit 7 starts it again (079B59 "LDB #$05,X; BPL", 079B5E "CLR #$08,X; CLR #$07,X; ANDB
# #$7F; STB #$05,X"); an animation's end may give the next one (079BA1 "STA #$05,X")
field object 05 animation u8
# what the animation did, cleared each time the sprite engine draws it (079AFF "CLR #$06,X"): bit 0 the animation ran
# to its end (079B90 "LDB #$06,X; ORB #$01"), bit 1 the frame is a marked one (079BCA "ORB #$02": the frame's byte
# 0 bit 4); set by others: bit 7 draws it again at once (0798C2 "LDA #$06,X; BMI"; 07D1A7 "ORA #$80" at a landing), bit
# 6 skips its drawing (0798C7 "ANDA #$40; BNE" then "CLR #$06,X")
field object 06 animation_flags u8
# the frame of the animation it shows: 079B3B "INC #$07,X" when the frame's time is out, 079B6D "LDA #$07,X; ASLA;
# ASLA; LEAU A,U" (4 bytes a frame), 079BAA "STA #$07,X" (a jump back)
field object 07 frame u8
# the frames the frame stays: 079B36 "LDA #$08,X; BNE" (none left: the next frame), 079BBF "STA #$08,X" from the
# frame's byte 1, 0798DE "DEC #$08,X"
field object 08 frame_time u8
# its sprites' attributes: bit 6 faces left (the sprites flipped: 079B49 "LDA #$09,X; ANDA #$40", 079B50 "LDA #$10;
# ORA <$F4"; the hit box's x offset the other way: 07C13A-07C1CE; 07D249 sets it from field 36), bits 4-5 the priority
# against the layers (079DE2 "LDA #$09,X; ANDA #$30"; from the floor map's cell: 07CDC2-07CDCF), bit 7 the colour in
# bits 0-3 instead of the frame's (079C1B "LDB #$09,X; BMI", 079C27 "ANDB #$0F")
field object 09 attributes u8
# the zoom of its sprites, from 10 (normal) up, when flags bit 4 is set (079C3A "BITA #$10; LBNE $9CD4"): 079CE1
# "LDB #$0A,X" into the sprite's horizontal zoom (and the steps its x offsets take: zoom_steps), 0B its vertical one
# (the defeated enemy's 07E118 "LDD #$0A,X; ADDD #$0101; STD #$0A,X" as it goes into the distance)
field object 0A zoom_x u8
field object 0B zoom_y u8
# where it is on the screen across: the mover adds field 0F (079978 "LDD #$0D,X; ADDD #$0F,X; STD #$0D,X", 079985
# "ADCA #$0C,X") and the camera's move (07998E "ADDD #$0C,X"); the sprites' x is it plus the frame's offset (079C4A "ADDD #$0C,X; STD
# #$06,Y"); a spawn sets it from its x less the camera (07CA04 "LDD #$00,X; SUBD <$AC; ADDD #$0040; STD #$0C,U")
field object 0C x u16
# its fraction (07CA1E "CLR #$0E,U")
field object 0E x_fraction u8
# its speed across, 8.8 (the mover; 07CC8E-07CC9E "STD #$0F,X" from a direction, the cosine)
field object 0F x_speed s16
# where it is on the floor, the screen's y: the mover adds field 14 (0799FC "LDD #$12,X; ADDD #$14,X", 079A09 "ADCA
# #$11,X") and the camera's move (079A12 "ADDD #$11,X"); the sprites' y is it plus z (079C53 "ADDD #$11,X", 079C56
# "ADDD #$16,X"); the depth sort orders the objects by it (079A44 "LDD #$11,X"); a spawn: 07CA21-07CA2E
field object 11 y u16
field object 13 y_fraction u8
# its speed on the floor, 8.8 (07CC92 "STD #$14,X" from a direction, the sine)
field object 14 y_speed s16
# its height: the mover adds field 19 (079A18 "LDD #$19,X; BEQ", 079A1D "ADDD #$17,X"); the landing puts it on the
# floor under it once it is no more than 7 above it (07D182 "LDD #$5C,X; ADDD #$0007", 07D18E "CMPD <$E8; BHI",
# 07D196 "LDD #$5C,X; STD #$16,X")
field object 16 z u16
field object 18 z_fraction u8
# its speed up, 8.8: gravity takes 0060 a frame off it (07D16E "LDD #$19,X; SUBD #$0060; STD #$19,X"), at most F800
# down (07D179 "CMPA #$F8"); 0 on landing (07D193 "CLRW #$19,X")
field object 19 z_speed s16
# its vitality: the setup gives it (07D147 "LDA #$04,U; STA #$1B,X"), a hit takes the hitter's damage off it
# (07C274 "LDA #$1B,X; SUBA #$1C,U; BCC; CLRA; STA #$1B,X"); at 0 the hit defeats it (0786B9's 07D0BE "LDA #$1B,X;
# BEQ")
field object 1B vitality u8
# its attack, the hit box's first word (07D1B7 "LDD ,Y; STD #$1C,X"): the damage it does (07C277 "SUBA #$1C,U") and
# the kind of hit it gives, which the victim keeps when it beats what hit it already this frame (07C2F1 "CMPA #$1D,U;
# BGT", 07C2F6 "LDA #$1D,U; STA #$1E,X")
field object 1C damage u8
field object 1D attack u8
# the strongest attack that hit it this frame (flags bit 5 set with it: 07C302 "ORA #$20"), cleared by the hit check
# of the enemies (07C115 "CLR #$1E,X"); 11-14 are the attacks the enemies' shared reactions answer (07CFF4 "LDA
# #$1E,X; SUBA #$11; CMPA #$03": 11 and 12 a flinch or a knock-down, 13 a spin, 14 a knock-back: 07D05C-07D0B0)
field object 1E hit u8
# its hit box, from the setup's hit box record (07D1B7-07D1CE: words 1F, 21, 23): the hit check (07C13A-07C1D7) takes
# two boxes as touching when, in each of y, x and z, the distance between the places plus the offsets is within the
# sum of the two sizes: 07C13A "LDB #$23,X" (y offset, signed) and 07C155 "LDB #$20,X; ADDB #$20,U" (depth); 07C162
# "LDB #$22,X" (x offset, the other way when it faces left) and 07C1A7 "LDB #$1F,X; ADDB #$1F,U" (width); 07C1B5
# "LDB #$24,X" (z offset) and 07C1CF "LDB #$21,X; ADDB #$21,U" (height)
field object 1F box_width u8
field object 20 box_depth u8
field object 21 box_height u8
field object 22 box_dx s8
field object 23 box_dy s8
field object 24 box_dz u8
# the object whose attack hit it (07C290 "STU #$25,X", 07C2C6 "STX #$25,U"); the shared hit routines read its kind,
# place and speed (07D004 "LDU #$25,X", 07D02A "LDU #$25,X; LDD #$0F,U", 07E21B "LDU #$25,X; LDD #$0F,U")
field object 25 hit_by u16 object
# the points it is worth (the setup's byte 5, 07D14D "LDA #$05,U; ANDA #$7F; STA #$27,X"): bits 0-3 the score to
# add, bits 4-5 the player who gets them (07CFC2 "LDA #$5B,U; ANDA #$70" from the hitter), bit 6 none; bit 7 set when
# it goes (07D0E0 "ORA #$80"), which 07BA50 turns into the score job of that player (07BA5D-07BA7B, then "CLR #$27,X")
field object 27 points u8
# what it does: the enemies' action, by which their states run a routine (07D62C "LDD #$28,X" with the banks' tables
# F620/F5A2; the shared reactions 0785FC/078602/07D667 "LDD #$28,X" 00-0C), and the action's step (29: each action
# switches on it, "INC #$29,X" to the next); the hit routines pick the reaction (07D090 "STA #$28,X", 07D093 "CLR
# #$29,X")
field object 28 action u8
field object 29 action_step u8
# its behaviour, the record of the actions it picks by the distance to its player (enemy_behaviour: 07D3D7-07D3FD
# reads its ranges, 07D604-07D624 its states); 07D42F "LDU #$F144", 07D432 "STU #$2A,X" the goon's
# (behaviour_choice gives the others': 030154 "LDD #$02,U; STD #$2A,X")
field object 2A behaviour u16
# the distance across and on the floor to the player it goes after (07D35B: 07D361 "LDD #$0C,U; SUBD #$0C,X", made
# positive, 07D36A/07D377 "STD #$2C,X"; 07D37A "LDD #$11,U; SUBD #$11,X", 07D383/07D390 "STD #$2E,X"); the
# behaviour's ranges are by them (07D3D7-07D3FD)
field object 2C target_dx u16
field object 2E target_dy u16
# what the record that puts it in gives it: a spawn's state byte (07C9FE "LDA #$05,X; STA #$30,U") or a child
# object's (07CA92 "LDD #$06,Y; STA #$30,U"); each type reads it as it starts (the story actors' script, 03E09D; bank
# 15's object's kind); the goons' shared routines then keep in it their place by their player (07D49C: 0 coming, 1 at
# its side, 2 waiting, 3 attacking)
field object 30 parameter u8
# what stops its walk (07CDE9-07CF5E, cleared at a spawn: 07CA44 "CLR #$31,U"): bit 7 a wall, bits 0-1 which way (80
# and 81 moving on the floor with a negative or positive y speed, 82 and 83 across: 07CEBB-07CEFC, then 07CEFE "ORA
# #$31,X; STA #$31,X"), bit 3 nowhere to go (07CE95 "ORA #$88"), bit 4 kept from the last frame (07CDE9 "ANDA #$10"),
# bit 5 a floor at another height, bit 6 in the air (07CDFC "ORA #$40" when z is not the floor's); 07CF5F turns it
# into the action that climbs (07CF86 "LDA #$31,X; ANDA #$07; STA #$28,X")
field object 31 blocked u8
# whether the hit came from behind: the hit check takes its facing (07D022 "LDA #$09,X; ANDA #$40; STA #$33,X") and
# turns it when the hitter pushes it the way it faces (07D030-07D041 by the hitter's x speed or place); the shared
# reactions pick the forward or backward one by it (07D071-07D0B0, 0786B9)
field object 33 hit_from_behind u8
# the way to the player it goes after (07D35B: 07D35E "CLR #$36,X", 40 when the player is to the left, turned by C0
# when it is lower, 20 when farther on the floor than across); 07D249 faces it that way (bit 6 of attributes when 36
# - 40 is not negative); 07D268 picks the walk's animation by it
field object 36 target_direction u8
# the player it goes after (07D301: the nearest one, by |dx| + |dy|, "STU #$38,X"; 07D4CA "STU #$38,X" the least
# chased one when that one has enough attackers); the enemies' routines measure the way to it (07D49C "LDU #$38,X",
# 07D49F "LBSR $D35B")
field object 38 target u16 object
# the frames until it looks for the nearest player again (07D4A2 "DEC #$3A,X; BNE", 07D4A7 "LDA #$10; STA #$3A,X");
# the goon's setup starts it at 10 (07D435 "LDA #$10; STA #$3A,X")
field object 3A retarget_time u8
# a countdown, of frames: the shared reactions (07DF3B "DEC #$3B,X; BNE", 07E0FC and 07E155 "DEC #$3B,X") and nearly
# every handler of the banks (227 of its writes in the C are a decrement) count it down
field object 3B timer u8
# the object it was born from (07CAAB "STX #$40,U": a child object put in at an offset from it)
field object 40 parent u16 object
# the hit box record the setup gave it (07D141 "STY #$48,X"), which the reactions put back when it gets up (07DDE9,
# 07E252, 07E2C5 "LDY #$48,X; LBSR $85B4"): a hit_box record's address in its bank
field object 48 hit_box u16
# where its sprites are in the sprite RAM: 8 entries of 0x10 bytes from 2000 + 80 x its number (07955F "LDU #$2000", 079572
# "STU #$-07,X" past the object, 079575 "LEAU #$0080,U"), kept when the slot is cleared (07CA64 "LDD #$59,U", 07CA78 "STD
# #$59,U"); the sprite engine writes them (07988E "LDU #$59,X", 079A91 "LDU #$59,X")
# bits 0-3 the shadow sprite drawn under it (079E10 "LDA #$5B,X; ANDA #$0F", shadow_sprites), bits 4-6 the player it
# belongs to (the players and what they throw: 03812D-038134 "ASLB" x4, "ORB #$5B,U; STB #$5B,U", 039216-03921A
# "ASLA" x4, "STA #$5B,U"), which a hit passes to the victim's points (07CFC2/07D044 "LDA #$5B,U; ANDA #$70")
field object 5B shadow_player u8
# the height of the floor under it, from the floor map (07CDBC "STA #$5D,X": the cell's low 4 bits x 8); a spawn
# sets it with z (07CA3E "STD #$5C,U"); its shadow is drawn there (079DFE "LDD #$5C,X; ADDD #$11,X"); it lands on it
# (07D182 "LDD #$5C,X")
field object 5C floor_z u16
# the next object in the same row of the depth sort (079A37: 079A68 "LDD #$5E,Y" to the row's last, 079A6D "STX
# #$5E,Y"; 079ACA "LDU #$5E,X", 079AD0 "STD #$5E,X" cleared as it is walked)
field object 5E draw_next u16 object

# ---- the families of this part ----
# the enemy spun away (actions 7 and 8): the x speed it is thrown with, kept to start it again after a wall (07E057
# "STD #$3E,X" here, 07DFE0 in action 7's start; 07E009 "LDD #$3E,X" into 0F in the shared step 07DFE7)
scoped object enemy_spin 3E spin_x_speed s16
# the enemies with their own hit animations (07865C, the step routines 07E1E8-07E2D6): whether the defeated one
# blinks out (not 0) or gets up again as a plain goon (0: 07E276 "LDA #$43,X; BNE"); the banks' setups set it (18
# times "LDA #$01; STA #$43,X", 10 times 0)
scoped object enemy_hurt 43 vanishes u8
# the sound queued on the marked frame of the defeated one's animation (07E289 "LDA #$06,X; ANDA #$02", 07E290
# "LDD #$4C,X; LBSR $97D3")
scoped object enemy_hurt 4C frame_sound u16
# the bosses' colours as they lose vitality (0786BF, the routine at 07E496): the palette effect's level, 5 unhurt
# (07E505 "LDA #$05", 07E507 "STA #$53,X" at the start, 07E4E4 "CMPA #$53,X; BCC": only a lower one counts), the
# palette job's slot (07E521 "STU #$54,X"; 0 none yet: 07E4A3 "LDU #$54,X"), the vitality it started with (07E50A
# "LDA #$1B,X", 07E50D "STA #$56,X")
scoped object boss_shade 53 shade_level u8
scoped object boss_shade 54 shade_job u16
scoped object boss_shade 56 full_vitality u8

# ======== files ========
# Replace the provisional lines 078000 unsorted/fixed_3C, 0791D8 unsorted/fixed_3C and 07E000 unsorted/fixed_3F
# (0786CE system/boot and 078F43 system/interrupts stay). The jump table's entries come first in the fixed program,
# each a routine or a jump to one: they stay together, as the original's table of entry points for the banks.
078000  file  system/jump_table    # the fixed program's entry points for the banks (an LBRA each) and the routines the decompiler folded into them
0791D8  file  system/inputs    # the coin slots, the credits and the players' controls, read at each IRQ
079269  file  video/clear    # clearing the K052109's three tile layers and the sprite RAM
079311  file  video/text    # the text printers: the game's texts, texts at an address, hex digits
079495  file  engine/floor    # the floor map (work RAM 4000): the cell under an object or where its speeds take it
079548  file  system/random    # the random number
07955F  file  engine/objects    # clearing the objects' slots, all of them or a list's
07960F  file  system/reset    # clearing the variables of a stage, of a game, and the scores
0796FD  file  game/score    # the players' scores and the high score table
079784  file  game/skip    # whether a player's button skips what is on (a story)
0797B7  file  system/jobs    # the queues: the main loop's jobs and the sound commands for the Z80, and the jobs themselves
079841  file  video/sprites    # the sprite engine: the objects' animations, their moves, the depth sort and their sprites
079E39  file  attract/sequence    # the attract mode: its scenes until a credit starts the game
07E010  file  enemies/reactions    # the enemies' shared reactions: spun away, defeated and knocked into the distance, fallen into a pit
07E18F  file  objects/fireman_goon_effect    # an object that shows kind 90's animation 11 once
07E1AE  file  enemies/hurt    # the hit reaction of the enemies with their own hit animations, and the plain goon they turn into

# ======== the jump table (078593-0786CB) ========
# Entries that only jump: vector_ and their routine's name (the routine is in fixed_3D/3E, named elsewhere, unless the
# comment names one of this file). The entries nothing calls keep their names (unused_vector_enemy_leave_side ...).

# ======== the boot (system/boot) ========
# the reset vector's routine (07FFFE reset_vector: 86CE; the test mode leaves through it, 05E3AA "LDX $FFFE; JMP ,X"):
# 0786D2 "LDA #$13; STA $7C00", the chips set up (1D00, 1FC2, 1FA4, 1FC0, 1D80/1F00, 1FB0-1FBC the K053251), 07870B
# "LDS #$5E00", the stack's RAM 5D00-5FFF tested with 00 55 AA FF (078760-078789; bad: 0789ED prints "11F BAD" three
# times, ram_check_bad_texts, waits and restarts), the work RAM (078798 "LBSR $8B11"), the RAMs cleared (07879E-0787F0),
# the FIRQ waited for (078814 "LDA <$56; BNE"), with the test switch held (078819 "LDA $1F81; ANDA #$01") the EEPROM
# test (game texts 6 EEP ROM TEST, 7 OK, 8 BAD, 9 RECOMMAND SET, A COMPLETE; bank 2F's 6000 and 6006), the flip
# setting (078892 "LBSR $6012"), the RAM ROM CHECK (0788A4 "LBSR $8B1C"), the palettes (0788C1-0788EA four 07BF51), the
# queues (078914-07893C), the high scores from default_high_scores (07893E-07894B: BAT HOM LIS MAR MAG INC SIM MAT FOX
# KON), the settings (078963 "LBSR $8A1A"), game state 1 (078966 "LDA #$01; STA <$00"), the interrupts on, then the
# main loop: 0789BC-0789C8 bank 20's 6003 each turn, 0789CB "LDX $4942; LDD ,X; BMI" a job waiting, 0789E4 "LDX #$E3FB;
# ASLA; JSR [A,X]" runs it by its number with B
0786CE  func  boot
comment boot The reset: sets the chips up, tests and clears the RAMs, runs the EEPROM test when the test switch is held, then the RAM ROM CHECK, loads the first palettes, sets the queues, the high score table and the settings, turns the interrupts on and runs the main loop: bank 20's background work and the jobs the queue holds, one at a time.
# the SWI and NMI vectors (FFFA, FFFC: 89EC), an "RTI": nothing raises them
0789EC  func  ignore_interrupt
comment ignore_interrupt Unused: the SWI and NMI vectors' routine; it returns at once and nothing raises them.
# 078A1A "LDX #$59F1; LDU #$E3EB; LDA ,X; LDA A,U" coinages by the coin setting (low nibble into <$1D/<$25, high into
# <$1C/<$24), 078A3A "LDA #$07,X" (59F8: 0 sets <$3B and <$39), 078A4F "LDA #$04,X; INCA" lives into <$5A, 078A56
# "LDA #$03,X" into <$14, 078A5C "LDA #$05,X" into <$13, 078A62 "LDA #$06,X" (the flip: 1E80, 1FA5 bits 0-1, the
# K053246's offsets 1FA0/1FA2 kept in <$86/<$89), 078ACD "LDB #$08,X" bit 2 of <$10, "LDA #$09,X" into <$3A
078A1A  func  apply_settings
comment apply_settings Takes the settings the test mode keeps at 59F1 into the game's variables: the coinage, the coin slots' mode, the lives, the difficulty, the sound in the attract, the screen flipped or not (the tile and sprite chips set for it), the coin counters' port bit and the first credit's extra coins.

078ADE  func  draw_boot_pattern
comment draw_boot_pattern Fills the text layer's middle, 36 tiles by 32 rows, with a pattern of tiles 2E 2F over 2C 2D.
# 078B11 "LDU #$4000; LDY #$0E80; LBSR $8DCF; TSTB"
078B11  func  check_work_ram
comment check_work_ram Tests the work RAM 4000-5CFF word by word; Z when it is good.
# the screen RAM ROM CHECK (game text B: 11F 1J 16G 16F 9G 8G 12C 13C 15C 16C 17C 6G 7G): 078B24 "LDA <$56; BNE"
# (the FIRQ), the RAMs by 1FC2 (078B29 "LDA #$06; STA $1FC2", 078B2F-078B84 LBSR $8DCF each, into 5D04-5D06; 5D07-5D08 by 078E19), the EEPROM by bank 2F's 600C (5D09), each printed OK or
# BAD (078BDC-078C1B, LBSR $8E7F each), the sums of the program's chips against rom_13c_sum ... rom_17c_sum (078C22-
# 078D0C), the Z80's check (078D23 "LBSR $8EB0": its ROM 6G with its sum, its RAM 7G), a wait (078D6D-078D80), then a
# restart when anything was bad (078D82 "TST $5D02")
078B1C  func  ram_rom_check
comment ram_rom_check The RAM ROM CHECK screen: tests the sprite, tile and palette RAMs and the EEPROM, adds up the program's four chips and checks them against their sums, asks the Z80 to check its ROM and RAM, prints OK or BAD by each chip and each sum, waits a while and restarts the game when anything was bad.
# 078D8C "LDA #$05; STA $1FC2" (the palette RAM in view), 078D92 "LDX #$0400" 15 x FFFF and 0000, 0420 16 x 001F
078D8C  func  set_check_colours
comment set_check_colours Sets the texts' colours for the RAM checks' screens: white (FFFF) at 0400, and red (001F) at 0420 for BAD.
# 078DBD "CLR <$F0; TSTB; BEQ; LDB #$40; STB <$F0", 078DC8 "LDD <$FA; LBSR $947D"
078DBD  func  print_rom_sum
comment print_rom_sum Prints the sum the check added up (48FA) as four hex digits at X, in red when B is not 0.
# 078DCF "LDX #$FFFF; STU $5D00", Y words written with X and read back (078DDE "STX ,U++", 078E02 "CMPX ,U++; BNE"), X
# less 5555 a pass: FFFF, AAAA, 5555, 0000 (078E0B "LEAX #$-5555,X", 078E0F "CMPX #$AAAB"); B 3 when a word differs
078DCF  func  test_ram_words
comment test_ram_words Tests Y words of RAM from U with the patterns FFFF, AAAA, 5555 and 0000: B 3 when one does not read back, else 0.

078E63  func  add_fixed_bytes

# 078E7F "ORB $5D02; STB $5D02", 078E8B "LDA #$04; STA $1FC2", 078E91 "LDX #$E41B" ("OK@" or, from 3 on, "BAD"), the

078E7F  func  print_check_result

# 078EB0 "LDD #$F181; STD $1FC6; TST $1FC4", up to 2000 reads of 1FC7 until it echoes 81 (078EC3 "CMPB $1FC7"), then

078EB0  func  ask_sound_cpu_check

# ======== the interrupts (system/interrupts) ========
# the IRQ vector (FFF8: 8F43), at each VBLANK: 078F63-078F74 the coins' inputs of the last three frames, the coin
# counters' pulses (078F7D-078FFB), the coin slots (078FFE-079034), the test switch (079037 "LDA $1F81; ANDA #$01":
# test mode), one sound command for the Z80 (079054-079070), then, unless the last IRQ's work is still running (079074
# "LDA <$12"), the frame count (079083 "INCW <$15"), the palette jobs (07908F "LBSR $BC8B"), the controls (079092-0790B3),
# the K052109's scrolls (0790B6-0790F0) and their copies (0790F4-07912D), the wait for the sprite DMA (079130 "LDA
# <$56; BNE"), the game state's routine (07913A "LDA <$00; ASLA; LDX #$E42B; JSR [A,X]": 0 the test mode, 1 the
# attract, 2 the game), 079143 "LBSR $C367" and 079146 "LBSR $9841" (the sprites)
078F43  func  irq_handler
comment irq_handler The IRQ's routine, at each frame: counts the coins and pulses the coin counters, enters the test mode when its switch is pressed, sends the Z80 one queued sound command, then reads the controls, sets the tile layers' scrolls, runs the palette jobs and the routine of the game's state (test mode, attract or game) and updates the sprites for the DMA.
# game state 0 (E42B's first): 079184 "LDX #$E431; LDA <$01; ASLA; JMP [A,X]": 0 07918D, 1 0791A2
079184  func  test_mode
comment test_mode The test mode's routine at each frame, by game_scene: its start, then bank 2F's test mode.
# 07918D "LBSR $9269; LBSR $9692", 079193-07919D the test mode's variables 5900-59EF cleared, 07919E "INC <$01"
07918D  func  test_mode_start
comment test_mode_start Starts the test mode: clears the tile layers, the scores and the game's variables, and the test mode's variables at 5900-59EF.
# 0791A2-0791AE "LDB #$2F; STB <$0E; SETLN <$0E", "LBSR $6009"
0791A2  func  test_mode_run
comment test_mode_run Runs a frame of bank 2F's test mode.
# the FIRQ vector (FFF6: 91B2), after the sprite DMA: 0791B2 "ORCC #$40", 0791B6-0791BE bit 2 of 1FC2 off (no more
# FIRQ), 0791C6-0791CE bit 4 of the K053246's register 5 off, 0791D4 "CLR <$56"
0791B2  func  firq_handler
comment firq_handler The FIRQ's routine, once the sprite DMA is over: turns the FIRQ and the K053246's interrupt off and clears dma_pending, which lets the next frame's sprites be written.

# ======== the coins and the controls (system/inputs) ========
# 0791D8 "LDB <$3D; ORB <$3E; COMB; ANDB <$3F; ANDB ,S" (the slot's bit A: in the input two frames ago, out in the

0791D8  func  coin_inserted
comment coin_inserted Whether a coin went through the coin slot whose bit is in A (released after being held): queues the coin's sound and counts it in coins_inserted; carry when it did.
# U the slot's record (4817 + 8 a slot): 0791F7 "INC #$02,U"; with <$3B clear (shared credits) 0791FF "INC #$03,U"
# (the counter's pulse) and 079202-079219 a credit each #$05,U coins, #$06,U credits into <$37; else 07921B-079244 the
# coins of 481C (and 483A more for the slot's first credit, "LDB #$07,U"), 481D credits into the slot's own word
0791F7  func  add_coin
comment add_coin Counts a coin in the coin slot's record at U and gives the credits it is worth when enough coins are in: into the shared credits, or into the slot's own when each slot has its credits (the first credit of a slot may take more coins).
# 079248 "LDA <$11; BNE" (the attract plays the demo's inputs instead)
079248  func  read_controls
comment read_controls Reads a player's controls from the port at U into its block at X, unless the attract runs.
# 07924D "LDA ,X; STA #$01,X" (last frame's), 079252 "LDA ,U; COMA; STA ,X" (this frame's), "LDA #$01,X; ANDA ,X;
# STA #$03,X" (held), "LDA #$01,X; COMA; ANDA ,X; STA #$02,X" (newly pressed)
07924D  func  update_controls
comment update_controls Updates a player's controls block at X from the port at U: this frame's, last frame's, the ones newly pressed and the ones held.

# sprites moved by its moves (07994C-07996E, 0799C7-0799F2 "ADDD #$0006,U", "#$0004,U"), 079978-079991 x, 0799FC-

# last (079A68 "LDD #$5E,Y", 079A6D "STX #$5E,Y"); then 079A7C-079AD7 the rows in order, each sprite's byte 1 a
# count from 1 (0 for the objects whose flags are not negative)
079A37  func  sort_objects_by_depth

079ADD  func  set_step_sprite_priority
comment set_step_sprite_priority Sets the sprites' default priority for the story's step.
# 079AE9: <$F7 1 when flags bit 3 (a shadow), <$F6 field 06, 079B03 the kind's set and bank (animation_sets), the
# frame's time (079B36), 079B3E "LDU #$6000" the set's index, attributes bit 6 (flipped), 079B59 the animation (bit 7
# again), 079B6D the frame (4 bytes: its sprites' count and flags, time, list), 079B90 the end (a jump to a frame or
# another animation), 079BD5 "LBSR $9DE2", 079BDB-079BEC an object lent when it needs more than 8 sprites (079CBD)
079AE9  func  draw_object
comment draw_object Steps the object's animation and writes its frame's sprites (and its shadow's) in the sprite RAM at Y, borrowing another object's sprites when it needs more than 8.
# 079C02: for each sprite of the list at U: its code (bit 15: flipped the other way), the colour (from the list or
# attributes' low nibble), its attributes, then its place from the object's (079C49-079C59), or zoomed (079CD4: the
# zoom from 0A/0B, its offsets by zoom_steps of bank 1D); 8 a slot, then the next lent object's (#$-02,Y); the rest of
# the slots cleared
079C02  func  write_object_sprites

# 079CBD "LDX #$55E0", down to 4D40: the first free (flags 0) taken with flags 1
079CBD  func  borrow_object_for_sprites
comment borrow_object_for_sprites Takes the last free object of the lists (from 55E0 down) to lend its sprites (flags 1); carry and X when there was one.
# 079DE2 "LDA #$09,X; ANDA #$30; BEQ", "LSRA; LSRA; STA <$FB" ...; else "LDA <$FA; STA <$FB"
079DE2  func  set_object_priority
