# ============================================================================================ left unnamed
# The original's mistakes, an extended address where the object's field was meant (symbols.txt notes each): 002F
# (03CD05 "DEC $002F", bear_change: the field 2F), 0031 (038A69/038A86 "TST $0031", player_throw_carried_4/5: the
# field 31), 003C (03C433 "STA $003C", football_player_start_rest: the field 3C), 00A0 (0212B9 "SUBD $00A0",
# bonus_results_draw_box), 00C0 (03C9D2 "ANDB $00C0", bear_break_out: the immediate C0). An io line names every
# constant of its value the C does not take for a number (X, Y and U loads, an address added to), and these values are
# everyday numbers there: the listing has 63 "#$00C0" (LEAX #$00C0,X: the players' stride), 14 "#$00A0", 4 "#$003C",
# 2 "#$002F"; a name such as meant_object_field_2f would replace them. So are 0C00 (palette_job_background_colour's
# "STD $0C00", the background's colour in the palette RAM: 9 "#$0C00", counts of the RAM test, Y loads in bank 1E) and
# 2000 (boot's clear of the sprite RAM: 27 "#$2000", the tile layers' "- 0x2000u").
# 24E2 and 26DD: places in the fixed layer's tiles the test mode writes once (05E193 "LDX #$24E2": the I/O check's
# blanked cells; 05E0B3 "LDX #$26DD": the ROM check's row), not variables.



# ======== the last object fields, and corrections ========
# ======== the 053248's last object fields still named after their offset, and corrections ========
# Evidence: build/listing/simpsons.s (quoted as PLACE "INSTRUCTION"), the C of src/ and the work list
# How the names reach the C here (read in tools/core): a function's own object (X) reads its family's fields only while
# the emitter knows X is still that object (decompiler/emit.py own_object: lost after a PULLS X or a call that may write
# X); otherwise the family comes from the pointer analysis, whose entry kinds carry no family in Konami
# (konami_cpu/decompile.py builds pointers.Program without families), so a "param FUNC x NAME object.FAMILY" line or a
# typed "local" at the instruction that writes the register gives it; a family's moved pointer (player + 0x60u) keeps
# the base's family (pointers.access, RUNS); an access by a constant address takes a family only through the profile's
# INSTANCE_FAMILIES_BY_FUNCTION (the "# instance" lines below); and Konami has no array fields (konami_cpu/emit.py:
# FIELD_ARRAYS and SCOPED_ARRAYS empty), so a structure's array is named one field per element.
# A line that changes an existing one has "# replaces: OLD LINE" right above it; where one old line becomes several new
# ones the replacement's other lines follow it, marked "(with the line above)".

# ======== the fields still unk_XX ========

# ---- 3D: carried, common ----
# What the engine does with byte 3D of every object: it clears it at every birth, with blocked (spawn_stage_objects
# 07CA41 "CLR #$3D,U" next to 07CA44 "CLR #$31,U"; place_child_object 07CAE5 "CLR #$3D,U"), and the players set it on
# whatever they pick up, of any kind (player_stand 038790 "LDA #$01; STA #$3D,X" on the object that touched it,
# player_eat_food 03942C "STB #$3D,Y" with B = 1): "carried" for the eight families that read it (throwable,
# bouncing_throwable, carried_obstacle, obstacle, running_animal, robot_scrap, bird_item, timed_throwable: their own
# lines say carried). The families that use the byte otherwise keep their own names (enemy way_round, player
# hold_presses, ...). Census: spawn_stage_objects and place_child_object "OBJECT(...)->unk_3D = 0u" (a new object is not
# carried); fat_goon_thrower_pick_up and unused_obstacle_fall too (both carried, see below)
field object 3D carried u8

# ---- 3D, 3E: the player's second sprite (the partner object at +60) ----
# player_second_sprite_start_prompt / _prompt / _blink get the player in U and work on its second sprite through
# U + 60 (03EBF0-03EC5D: "#$0090,U", "#$009D,U", "#$009E,U", "#$60,U": the partner's 30, 3D, 3E, 00). As the player
# family's view (the moved pointer keeps it) 3E already reads blink_frames, as the player code reads the same byte
# (player_team_ready 0391A4 "CLR #$009E,U" before "LDA #$03; LDY #$B180; LBSR $7C2F": state 3, the blinking picture);
# 3D is not hold_presses there but the prompt's frames: 03EC02 "LDA #$01; STA #$009D,U" (state 5 starts it at 1),
# 03EC0B "DEC #$009D,U; BEQ" (at 0: "LDA #$3C; STA #$009D,U", 60 frames, and picture B180), 03EC11 "LDA #$009D,U; CMPA
# #$1E" (at 30: picture B181): the two prompts (Hit Buttons!, Wiggle Joystick!) alternate every 30 frames. A family of
# its own, player_second_sprite, whose view takes the player's fields (NESTED_FAMILIES) but this one. The functions
# player_second_sprite_* then belong to it (their X is never an object: 03EAB3 "LDX #$7E5B; JMP [A,X]", and
# player_second_sprite_fall's X is a place), and nothing in them reads the player's own 3D
scoped object player_second_sprite 3D prompt_frames u8
param player_second_sprite_start_prompt u player object.player_second_sprite
param player_second_sprite_prompt u player object.player_second_sprite
param player_second_sprite_blink u player object.player_second_sprite

# ---- 43-58: the story actor's child slots, one field each ----
# Konami has no array fields (a structure laid out backwards: konami_cpu/emit.py), so "child_actors u16[B]" names only
# its first word. The 11 slots (story_actor_put_in 03E398 "LEAX #$43,X; LDD ,X; BNE; STU ,X", 03E3A6 "DEC <$F0" from
# 0B; story_actor_finish_frame 03E68D, story_actor_remove 03E71C, story_actor_remove_children 03E7A9 walk them by

# ---- 07: an attack range's chances and actions, counted from 1 (not an object field) ----
# enemy_think 07D5D9 "LEAU #$07,U" (U one before the range's action_chances), 07D5DC "SUBA B,U" with B 4 down to 1
# (action_chances[B - 1]); 07D5E5 "LEAU #$-04,U" (one before its actions), 07D5E8 "LDA B,U; STA #$28,X" (actions[B -
# 1]). The C reads them as ATTACK_RANGE(range + choice - 7)->unk_07 and ATTACK_RANGE(range + choice - 3)->chance (the
# range's own chance, wrong): a record pointer moved inside the record has no array to land in (no array fields in
# Konami). The same in the state's choice: 07D614 "LEAU #$03,U", 07D617 "SUBA B,U" (the state record's chances 4-7),
# 07D621 "LEAU #$-03,U", 07D624 "LDA B,U" (its actions 1-4), C "mem_read8(state_record + choice)", "mem_read8(state_record
# - 3u + choice)". As values a pointer walks (elements, read through data_record as the records are) the C reads
# BEHAVIOUR_CHANCE(range_chances + choice) and BEHAVIOUR_ACTION(range_actions + choice)
elements behaviour_chance u8
elements behaviour_action u8
# replaces: local enemy_think 07D5C3,07D5C6,07D5D9,07D5E5 u range
local enemy_think 07D5C3,07D5C6 u range
# (with the line above)
local enemy_think 07D5D9 u range_chances behaviour_chance
local enemy_think 07D5E5 u range_actions behaviour_action
# replaces: local enemy_think 07D60D,07D614 u state_record
local enemy_think 07D60D u state_record
# (with the line above)
local enemy_think 07D614 u state_chances behaviour_chance
local enemy_think 07D621 u state_actions behaviour_action

# ======== what the carry a routine hands back says ========
# What the carry of a routine says where it hands it back ('flag FUNCTION cy NAME'); the functions that only hand it on
# from these, and the callers whose carry only comes from them, take the name too (konami_cpu/decompile.py
# inherited_flag_names)
# stage_boss_any_player_down: carry 1 when a player in play is in a state its class marks negative (down, hurt)
flag stage_boss_any_player_down cy player_down
# stage_boss_blink_out: carry 1 once the blinks are done and the boss is removed (its score awarded)
flag stage_boss_blink_out cy gone

# ======== what the flags say, the last register names ========
# ---- system ----
# group system: flags and register variables of src/system, src/engine, src/video, src/game, src/attract,
# src/test_mode (proposals; symbols.txt syntax)

# ======== flag sources ========

# --- src/engine/floor.c ---
# floor_cell_at: the floor map's cell is read last (079545 "LDA ,U; RTS"): N is its bit 7, which the floor map sets
# where there is no floor ("its value in A (negative: no floor)"; scenery_block_floor writes FF there to take the floor
# away; check_floor_ahead "BMI" on the cell ahead stops the object before a gap)
flag floor_cell_at s no_floor
# check_floor_ahead: 07CF4C "LDA #$42,X; BMI $CF5E; BEQ $CF5E": Z set when the object's enemy_class is 0 (the C:
# "zero = enemy_class == 0u; if ((int8_t)enemy_class >= 0 && zero == 0u)")
flag check_floor_ahead z no_enemy_class
# done: src/engine/floor.c
# done: src/engine/directions.c

# --- src/game/score.c ---

# ======== caller exceptions (callees that mean different things, one test in the caller) ========

# once for that ("carry when there was a free slot")

# ======== callers whose only source can not carry a name ========
# Each source below hands back a flag its own variable also uses for something else (an arithmetic carry, a shift's
# carry handed to table overrun cases, or other tests), so no flag line can be given to it and the name can not come
# up by itself; each caller here gets the flag only from it (calls whose flag nothing reads after them aside) and
# tests it for that one thing.
#
# boxes_overlap (its carry is also the ADDB/ADCA carry of the half sizes added, 07C154.. "ADDB #$20,U; ADCA #$00"):
# 07C1DA "CMPD <$F6; BCC $C1DE", 07C1DC "CLRA; RTS", 07C1DE "COMA; RTS": carry set when the two boxes overlap. Callers:
# 07C058/07C08F/07C0C7/07C129/07C1F9 "LBSR $C13A; BCC" then the trade of hits (players_touch for the players' pairs)
flag collide_players_with_enemies cy overlapping
flag collide_players_with_child_objects cy overlapping
flag collide_players_with_list_1_objects cy overlapping
flag unused_collide_with_list_1_objects cy overlapping
flag collide_players_with_players cy overlapping
# stage_boss_move_on_screen (its variable is the carry of the x sum, 03C0EB..; it ends in stage_boss_follow_floor or
# stage_boss_stop_on_floor, which hand on stage_boss_settle's landed): callers 03CC47 "LBSR $60EB; LBCC $6CD9"
# (bear_knocked_down: its vector_spawn_child carries are read by nothing), 03D497 "LBSR $60EB; LBCS $7285", 03D4A7
# "LBSR $60EB; BCS $74AD", 03C76A "LBSR $60EB; BCC $6769", 03C772 "LBSR $60EB; BCC $67AB": each goes on once landed
flag bear_knocked_down cy landed
flag stage_3_boss_leap cy landed
flag stage_3_boss_knocked cy landed
flag football_player_knocked_back cy landed
flag football_player_knocked_out cy landed
# burns_part_fall (its variable is also the carry of the height's sum, 03B6DD "ADCA #$16,X"): 03B6EA "CLRA; RTS"
# above the floor, 03B6F3 "COMA; RTS" put on the floor; burns_debris_bounce 03B6AD "LBSR $76CA; BCC $76C9" bounces
# when it lands
flag burns_debris_bounce cy landed
# krusty_balloon_throw (its variable also takes the ASLA carry of the side handed to the table overrun cases,
# "carry = (int8_t)side_index < 0;"): carry set when neither list 1 nor list 2 has room for the shot ("carry = 1u;"

# ======== the stack slots and temporaries ========
# ---- system ----
# group system: the 053248 C's stack slots and temporaries in src/system, src/engine, src/video, src/game,
# src/attract, src/test_mode, src/scenes, src/stages (proposals; symbols.txt syntax)
#
# A note on the plain `stack` the C shows: emit.renumbered() renames the first of a function's numbered names
# (stack_1, stack_10, stack_10001...) to its base when the base is free, so the C's `stack` is a slot too; the work
# list (which looks for stack_N) misses it. Its slot is named here with the rest, by the store that writes it.

# stack_2 << 8) | stack;", then the record's lives). s2 its high byte, s1 its low byte
local demo_start 07A0EA s2 saved_player_high

# 03A150 "LSRB; BCC" (the players' bits), 03A153 "PUSHS B" ... 03A15F "PULLS B"; 03A163 "PUSHS B" ... 03A16F "PULLS B":
# the bits kept around the distance checks
local stage_8_boss_player_is_close 03A153,03A163 s1 saved_player_bits
# 03A3B5 "PUSHS A" (the angle to walk), 03A3BD "LDB A,Y" (stage_8_boss_walk_speeds_by_players), 03A3BF "PULLS A",
# 03A3C1 "LBSR $8617" (vector_set_speed_by_direction)
local stage_8_boss_phase_1 03A3B5 s1 saved_angle
# 03A458 "PUSHS A" (the run speed), 03A45A "LBSR $863B" (vector_floor_ahead), 03A45E "PULLS A; BPL; NEGA"
local stage_8_boss_phase_2 03A458 s1 saved_run_speed
# 03A68D "PUSHS X" (the boss, around the palette request), later "PULLS X"
local stage_8_boss_take_hits 03A68D s2 saved_boss
# 03A95C "LDD ,Y", 03A95E "PUSHS D", 03A960 "ADDD ,Y" x3, 03A966 "ADDD ,S++; ADDD #$3711": the old value, 5 times it
# plus 3711 the next
local stage_8_boss_next_random 03A95E s2 old_value
# 03A991 "LDD #$0F,X; ABSD", 03A995 "PUSHS D", 03A99B "ADDD ,S++" (the y speed's size)
local stage_8_boss_speed 03A995 s2 x_speed_size
# done: src/objects/stage_8_boss.c

# ---- src/players/gauges.c ----

local gauges_draw 040907 s1 player_counter

local continue_end 040B26 s10006 saved_caller_byte

# the slot holds the player's low byte, then the tiles still to draw

# 040AA8 "LEAS #$-10,S", 040AAB "STA #$00,S" (the count, BCD), 040ABE "LDA #$00,S; ANDA #$F0" (tens), 040AE9 "LDA #$00,S;

local continue_draw_count 040B48 s1 seconds_bcd

local gauges_put_picture 040B88 s1 blank_flag
# 040BD6 "ANDA #$7F", 040BD8 "STA #$06,S", 040BE1 "LDA #$06,S; ASLA; LDD A,X" (gauge_player_columns)
local gauge_draw_picture 040BD8 s10 quarter_number
# done: src/players/gauges.c

# ======== the closing's fixes ========
# the object's own z, compared with its floor: 0386F5 "LDX #$16,U; CMPX #$5C,U" (the code the players' standing, walking
# and team states share), 03892F (player_start_move) and 03945F (player_take_blow) the same; the C had named it floor_z
# after the field it is compared with
local player_walk 0386F5 x player_z
local player_team_jump 0386F5 x player_z
local player_team_start_fall 0386F5 x player_z
local player_attack_end 0386F5 x player_z
local player_team_together 0386F5 x player_z
local player_team_move 0386F5 x player_z
local player_team_fall 0386F5 x player_z
local player_start_move 03892F x player_z
local player_take_blow 03945F x player_z
# player_start_jump_attack gets that z in X (its callers' player_z), which it keeps in its stack slot player_z
param player_start_jump_attack x z

# the stage bosses' shared routines' phase and wait, as the bear's and the football player's own: stage_boss_set_state
# 03C055 "STY #$2E,X" (the state and its wait), stage_boss_blink_out counts the blinks down in 2F
scoped object stage_boss 2E phase u8
scoped object stage_boss 2F wait u8

local burns_robot_aim_at_target 03B2B9,03B2C6 x object object.burns_robot
